assumed_causal_direction: higher node quality -> higher suitability; specialists penalised more by low quality; managed-only nodes add captivity-tolerance bonus and migration-need penalty
parameters: q_j, breadth_s, spec_s, tol_s, mig_s; literals 0.72,0.28,0.32,0.25,0.24
rationale: Linear niche-quality mapping is a common phenomenological habitat-suitability device; captivity tolerance and migration need encode qualitative ex situ suitability differences
supporting_references: No direct calibration; qualitative motivation from ex situ literature (Conde et al. 2011; Pritchard et al. 2012; Redford et al. 2012)
plausible_alternatives: logistic/threshold suitability; multiplicative niche x quality; species-specific climate envelopes
annual_sequence_position: A1 step 4 (true and observed); reused by A2
role_in_S6_S7: drives movement eligibility (s<0.58), target scoring, survival (E11) and births (E12) -> central to both arms
existing_sensitivity_evidence: LHS does not vary the literals; sweeps vary quality drivers only
limitations: literals not varied; no species-specific climate response (climate_sensitivity inert)

ecological_phenomenon: Habitat quality dynamics (deterioration, climate displacement, restoration, catastrophes, collapse)
assumed_causal_direction: deterioration and climate lower origin quality; habitat spend raises all wild-node quality in proportion to restoration potential; catastrophes reduce random wild node
functional_form: q_j(t)=clip(q_j(t-1) - trend - [j=0] v t/T + [j=1] 0.65 v t/T + (habitat_spend/B0) e r_j - catastrophe; 0.05,0.98); collapse -0.70 at year T/3 (collapse scenario)
rationale: Represents directional degradation and partial restorability of wild habitat
supporting_references: qualitative: Hoegh-Guldberg et al. 2008; Thomas 2011; Watson et al. 2014
plausible_alternatives: linear cumulative climate shift (displacement proportional to t, not increments proportional to t); saturating restoration; spatially correlated catastrophes
role_in_S6_S7: the S6-S7 reversal is decided by the race between E2 decline and habitat-spend recovery (S6 habitat share 0.68 vs S7 0.35)
existing_sensitivity_evidence: LHS: deterioration, climate_velocity, habitat_protection_efficiency; sweeps deterioration_relocation, climate_assisted_risk, engagement_habitat; ablation climate
limitations: per-year climate decrement grows with t, so cumulative displacement is quadratic in t (~0.61 at year 100 for v=0.012); manuscript text states 0.012 t/100 without this distinction; restoration is linear and unbounded below cap
assumption_class: Mechanistic simplification; functional form not justified

assumed_causal_direction: managers see lognormal-noised counts of visible species and one-year-delayed noisy quality
functional_form: n_obs = n_true x LogNormal(0,0.18) for stage>=2 else NA; q_obs = clip(q(t-1)+N(0,0.10);0,1)
rationale: Monitoring error and reporting lag are standard in adaptive management
supporting_references: Williams & Brown 2022; Chades et al. 2021 (framing only)
role_in_S6_S7: decision inputs to A2 for S1-S5, S7
limitations: noise magnitudes synthetic

ecological_phenomenon: Discovery of latent species (5-stage knowledge progression)
assumed_causal_direction: survey spend and detectability raise per-stage advance probability; species visible to decisions at stage>=2
functional_form: P(advance from k)=min(cap_k, b + c_k (survey_spend/survey_cost) [x detect at k=0] [+habitat_spend/1000 at k=4])
rationale: Represents detection-then-recognition delay of undescribed taxa
supporting_references: Mora et al. 2011; Tedesco et al. 2014; Liu et al. 2022; Boehm & Cronk 2021 (qualitative)
role_in_S6_S7: gates which species can be moved; largest load-bearing component of Psi (ladder)
role_in_Psi: M3 surrogate: cohort joins movable pool at expected discovery year
existing_sensitivity_evidence: sweep latent_survey; ablation latent_species; EBD boundary audit
limitations: stage coefficients synthetic; at most one stage/year

assumed_causal_direction: fixed policy shares split current budget across seven channels
functional_form: spend_c = B_t a(pi,c)/max(sum a,1)
rationale: Policies are archetypes of how one budget is split
supporting_references: Joseph et al. 2009 (allocation framing)
role_in_S6_S7: S6 vs S7 differ in all seven shares (bundled contrast)
limitations: bundling of allocation with movement rule

assumed_causal_direction: rescue spend buys moves; individuals of at-risk visible species in low-suitability nodes are eligible
functional_form: C=max(1,floor(rescue/2.5)); eligible if decision suitability<0.58 (S2/S4/S5/S7); S1 managed-only; S3 refuge/return thresholds; take=min(cands, C-moved, max(1,floor(cands/5)), target space)
parameters: 2.5 cost per move, 0.58, 20% take, s3 thresholds 0.48/0.62/delay 5
rationale: Translocation is capacity-limited and triggered by perceived habitat inadequacy
supporting_references: Seddon et al. 2014; Dickens et al. 2010
plausible_alternatives: cost per move by distance/node; optimisation over moves
role_in_S6_S7: core of the circulation channel C
role_in_Psi: M3 shares capacity as equal quota
limitations: 2.5 and 0.58 and 20% are literals not varied; max(1,...) gives at least one move even at tiny spend

assumed_causal_direction: higher suitability, lower cost, higher research and (S7) restoration raise target attractiveness; origin fidelity bonus
functional_form: score_j = s_obs(sp,j) - 0.04 cost_j + 0.03 research_j + bonuses + origin_fidelity[j=0]; biobank -1
parameters: 0.04, 0.03, S4 +0.10 managed-transitional, S7 +0.08 restoration +0.05 research, origin_fidelity 0.20
rationale: Encodes manager preference ordering
supporting_references: none (normative)
plausible_alternatives: multi-criteria with explicit weights from stakeholders
limitations: no network topology/connectivity constraint

ecological_phenomenon: Relocation stress, movement and release mortality
assumed_causal_direction: moving lowers health (buffered by stress tolerance); movement and managed->wild release kill a fraction
functional_form: health*=1-0.10(1-tol_i); P(die move)=0.025; P(die release)=0.08
rationale: Translocation stress and post-release mortality are well documented
supporting_references: Dickens et al. 2010; Jule et al. 2008; Harrington et al. 2013
existing_sensitivity_evidence: LHS relocation_mortality, relocation_stress, release_survival_penalty; adverse high_relocation_harm
limitations: release counter recorded before release mortality

assumed_causal_direction: moved susceptibles may be infected; quarantine coverage reduces risk
functional_form: P=0.03(1-0.65 cov), cov=min(1,rescue/(0.25 moved))
rationale: Translocation disease risk
supporting_references: Kock et al. 2010
limitations: quarantine cost not deducted from move budget

assumed_causal_direction: frequency-dependent infection within node; recovery to permanent immunity
functional_form: P(inf)=clip(beta_j x prevalence_j;0,0.65); P(recover)=0.32
rationale: Simple SIR-type frequency dependence
supporting_references: Kock et al. 2010 (qualitative)
limitations: annual time step coarse for epidemics

assumed_causal_direction: survival falls with intrinsic mortality, low suitability, anthropogenic pressure, infection, predation (wild), poor health, inbreeding; rises with research in managed nodes
functional_form: p=clip(1-mort_s mu-(1-suit)0.24-press 0.08-0.14 I+0.035 M research-0.035 W pred mu_p-0.08(1-health)-0.08 F;0.05,0.995)
rationale: Additive hazard decomposition is transparent
supporting_references: Araki et al. 2007; Frankham 2008 (direction of inbreeding/captivity effects)
existing_sensitivity_evidence: LHS mortality multipliers only via adverse designs
limitations: age-independent, no senescence; floor 0.05

assumed_causal_direction: births per co-located mature female increase with growth+mortality, fertility, suitability; decrease with species-specific crowding, infection, inbreeding; ex situ spend boosts managed-node fecundity
functional_form: births~Poisson(n_F rate), rate=(mort+growth)(0.5+fert) suit max(0.05,1-n_sj/K_j) 5.0 (1+0.22 exsitu/B)[M] max(.05,1-0.30 inf) max(.05,1-0.35 Fbar); requires >=1 mature F and M at node
rationale: (mort+growth) scaling makes replacement roughly balanced at good suitability; mate limitation via co-location
supporting_references: Snyder et al. 1996 (captive breeding limits, qualitative)
plausible_alternatives: Beverton-Holt/Ricker density dependence; shared node capacity across species; Allee effects
role_in_S6_S7: ex situ benefit is a key S7 lever
role_in_Psi: M3 with female fraction and min breeding pop
existing_sensitivity_evidence: LHS ex_situ_breeding_benefit; sweep captivity_breeding; cap audit
limitations: 5.0 scaling literal; density uses species count over whole node capacity (no interspecific competition); births truncated in species-index order under cap

assumed_causal_direction: same-founder matings raise offspring inbreeding; diversity-aware paternity (genetics spend>0) avoids same founder and reduces inbreeding by 18%
functional_form: F_child=0.5(F_m+F_f)+0.08[same founder]; x0.82 if diversity-aware; founder lineage inherited from one parent
rationale: Captures direction of pedigree management benefit
supporting_references: Frankham 2008; Williams & Hoffman 2009; Howell et al. 2021
limitations: not a population-genetic model; no adaptation to captivity

assumed_causal_direction: hard computational cap on living individuals
functional_form: births truncated when sum alive = 1200
rationale: Computational convenience
supporting_references: none
limitations: truncation order favours low species index

assumed_causal_direction: stock decays 1%/yr and grows with biobank share for extant visible species
functional_form: b_s=clip(b_s(1-0.01)+0.05 biobank/B;0,1)
rationale: Represents genetic-resource banking as an option
supporting_references: Bolton et al. 2022; Howell et al. 2021
limitations: biobank never restores individuals; biobank_future_value config unused

assumed_causal_direction: a latent species lost while stage<2 is an EBD
functional_form: EBD if not extant and not known and stage<2
rationale: Endpoint defined on model visibility rule
supporting_references: Boehm & Cronk 2021; Tedesco et al. 2014
limitations: model-defined endpoint

assumed_causal_direction: node welfare standard minus captivity, predation, food insecurity, crowding, restriction, infection, habituation, relocation burdens
functional_form: w_i=welfare_j - 0.12 M(1-tol_i) - sum_k burden_k
rationale: Five Domains-inspired additive decomposition
supporting_references: Mellor et al. 2020; Beausoleil et al. 2018
limitations: normative device; does not feed back on demography

assumed_causal_direction: visitor exposure, engagement spend and habitat signal raise engagement; next-year budget rises with engagement
functional_form: eng=clip(eng+0.08(exposure+0.2 eng_spend/B)+0.02 hbar;0,1.5); B_{t+1}=B0(0.82+0.24 eng)
rationale: Represents public-support funding feedback
supporting_references: Moss et al. 2015 (qualitative)
plausible_alternatives: engagement that can decline (welfare scandals, fatigue); lagged funding
role_in_S6_S7: policy-dependent budget via exposure (S7 moves animals into high-exposure nodes)
existing_sensitivity_evidence: LHS engagement_coefficient (can be negative); sweep engagement_habitat; ablation human_feedback
limitations: with default positive coefficients engagement is non-decreasing and saturates; 'funding collapse' (x0.72) is overwritten next step, i.e. a one-year shock

assumed_causal_direction: fixed order: funding, allocation, environment, observation, discovery, movement, disease, survival, ageing, reproduction, biobank/EBD, welfare, engagement, logging
functional_form: sequential; within-step updates vectorised (synchronous) except movement (species processed in descending risk order, asynchronous capacity depletion)
rationale: Management acts on last-observed state before demography
supporting_references: Grimm et al. 2020 (scheduling guidance)
role_in_S6_S7: order fixes that moves precede survival and births
limitations: no test of alternative order

ecological_phenomenon: Action selection (risk ranking, eligibility, target, take)
assumed_causal_direction: most at-risk visible species served first until capacity exhausted
functional_form: risk=1/(1+n_obs)+(1-s_obs at origin); eligibility, target and take as E6-E7
rationale: Triage heuristic
supporting_references: Joseph et al. 2009; McCarthy & Possingham 2007 (framing)
limitations: heuristic, not optimal
